summary.headline: Two concurrent shocks hitting the book: (1) an AI-capex-sustainability selloff after TSMC raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B, hitting MRVL -8.6% (persisting RED, -31% over the month), CRDO -8.1% (persisting RED), AMD -5.2% and LRCX -4.3% (both AMBER); (2) Bitcoin's slide toward $60K on persistent spot-ETF outflows, hitting HUT -10.7% and MARA -6.8% (both escalated to RED on direct thesis match) and HOOD -8.2% (new RED). CWAN roster-integrity flag is now unresolved for a 3rd consecutive run — still listed in portfolios.json 22 days after delisting. Also note: a 17-day gap since the last Sentinel run (06-30 → 07-17) means several of today's reads are first looks, not continuous tracking. One bright spot: ABT +10.7% on a Q2 beat-and-raise, and the STLD margin-compression AMBER from 06-30 appears to have been wrong — STLD's own July guidance shows margin expansion, not compression; downgrading to resolved/green.

flags.headline: HUT -10.66%: Bitcoin slide toward $60K directly hits crypto-treasury thesis risk
flags.detail: Hut 8 fell -10.66% ($102.97→$91.99), now down roughly 30% over six weeks per Benchmark's Mark Palmer (who nonetheless doubled his price target to $165 on 'strong operating momentum' ahead of Q2). No HUT-specific negative catalyst identified — the move tracks the broader Bitcoin decline (spot ETFs on an 8-week net-outflow streak, ~$8.2B cumulative, BTC pinned near $60-64K). Q2 report pending; River Bend data center buildout execution remains the other watch item.
flags.thesis_link: Matches HUT key_risk #3: 'Bitcoin price exposure remains significant — average revenue per BTC mined fell 17% YoY, and $295.7M in digital asset losses in Q1 demonstrate the volatility of the crypto treasury strategy.' Sustained Bitcoin weakness is that risk materializing; escalated to RED on thesis match.

evidence.source: MarketBeat — HUT shares gap down
FXLeaders — Bitcoin ETF $4.5B June outflow, BTC $64.1K

flags.headline: MARA -6.84%: Bitcoin weakness continues to compress the thesis's existential risk case
flags.detail: MARA Holdings fell -6.84% ($12.28→$11.44). No new company-specific news; the move is consistent with the broader crypto drawdown (Bitcoin near $60-64K, spot ETFs on an extended outflow streak). MARA already carried a Q1 EPS-miss AMBER flag as of 06-30; this is a further leg down in the same underlying risk.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk #1: 'Persistent GAAP losses ($1.3B in Q1 2026 alone) driven by Bitcoin price volatility... create existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn and the company cannot service its $850M convertible debt obligations.' Direct match — escalated AMBER (06-30) → RED.

evidence.source: CNBC — Bitcoin set to slump to new 2026 lows after recent sell-off
FXLeaders — Bitcoin ETF $4.5B June outflow

flags.headline: HOOD -8.15%: falling back below the $100 support zone on credit-expansion scrutiny plus crypto-revenue drag
flags.detail: Robinhood fell -8.15% ($115.47→$105.58), retreating toward the $100 level after failing to hold above $120 earlier this month. Investors are scrutinizing the company's push into consumer credit (a new premium card, reportedly preparing to sell up to $500M in asset-backed securities) as raising operational/credit risk, compounding the existing crypto-revenue softness (crypto revenue was already down 47% YoY per HOOD's own report) as Bitcoin slides toward $60K.
flags.thesis_link: Matches HOOD key_risk #1: 'Q1 2026 revenue decelerated to 15% YoY while crypto revenue collapsed 47%, demonstrating exposure to volatile trading volumes.' Continued Bitcoin weakness is that risk persisting; the new credit-expansion angle is an incremental, not-yet-in-thesis concern worth watching separately. Escalated to RED on thesis match + technical breakdown toward a round-number support level.

evidence.source: FXLeaders — Robinhood slides toward $100 on credit expansion, fundraising scrutiny

flags.headline: MRVL -8.60%: extends to -31% over the month as TSMC's capex hike reignites AI-ROI worries
flags.detail: Marvell fell -8.60% ($206.22→$188.48), now down ~31% over the past month per 24/7 Wall St. The proximate trigger is TSMC raising its 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B (from $52-56B) — framed by some analysts as bullish demand confirmation, but the market read it as a signal that capex growth may be outrunning near-term ROI, dragging Broadcom, AMD, Intel and Micron down alongside MRVL. This is the same AI-capex-moderation risk flagged persistently since late June; still no analyst downgrades (consensus remains Buy, 28 analysts).
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk #1: 'Forward P/E of 53.3x... after a ~150% stock price surge embed extraordinary growth expectations; any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target or moderation in hyperscaler AI capex would trigger severe multiple compression.' Persisting RED since 2026-06-28.

evidence.source: 247WallSt — Marvell drops 8% as AI capex slowdown fears weigh on chips
GuruFocus — TSMC lifts 2026 capex to $64B

flags.headline: CRDO -8.12%: same AI-capex-sustainability rout as MRVL; valuation leaves no margin for error
flags.detail: Credo Technology fell -8.12% ($226.66→$208.26) in the same TSMC-capex-triggered chip selloff that hit MRVL, Broadcom, AMD and Intel. Credo carries the least cushion of the group — 109x trailing / 39x forward P/E after a 90% YTD run — so it is the most exposed to any re-rating on AI capex-ROI questions. Consensus remains Strong Buy.
flags.thesis_link: Matches CRDO key_risk #1: 'Extreme valuation — 109x trailing P/E and 39x forward P/E... embed aggressive growth expectations, leaving minimal margin of safety for any execution miss or AI capex slowdown.' Persisting RED since 2026-06-28.

evidence.source: 247WallSt — Marvell drops 8% as AI capex slowdown fears weigh on chips (sector-wide)

flags.headline: AMD -5.19%: caught in the same TSMC-capex-driven chip selloff
flags.detail: AMD fell -5.19% ($528.80→$501.34) as part of the broad semiconductor selloff (Broadcom -3%, Intel -5%, iShares Semiconductor ETF -4%) following TSMC's capex guidance hike. No AMD-specific negative news; this is sector contagion on a name with strong underlying fundamentals (BUY, score 85) and zero margin-of-safety valuation.
flags.thesis_link: Matches AMD key_risk #1: 'Forward P/E of 59.8x and 270% 52-week appreciation leave zero margin of safety — any AI spending deceleration or customer pause would trigger severe multiple compression.'

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance — Marvell drops 8% as AI capex slowdown fears weigh on chips; Broadcom, AMD, Intel slide

flags.headline: LRCX -4.29%: WFE cyclicality risk re-asserting alongside the broader chip selloff

flags.thesis_link: Matches LRCX key_risk #1: 'Inherent cyclicality of the semiconductor equipment industry... the current AI-driven super-cycle could reverse if AI capital spending moderates.'

evidence.source: 247WallSt — Marvell drops 8% as AI capex slowdown fears weigh on chips (sector-wide)

flags.thesis_link: Matches COIN key_risk #2: 'Revenue concentration in crypto trading volumes makes Coinbase a leveraged bet on crypto market sentiment.' Not escalated to RED — move is moderate, not extreme.

flags.headline: QCOM -3.98%: caught in chip-sector contagion; the thesis itself has shifted since the 06-30 memory-shortage flag
flags.detail: Qualcomm fell -3.98% to $170.75, part of the broad semiconductor pullback. Note the underlying story has moved since the last Sentinel run: the current screener report (updated since 06-30) no longer lists the memory-shortage / handset-production risk that drove the prior RED flag — QCOM's key_risks now center on Chinese customer weakness and Apple modem-internalization risk instead, and the report's recommendation improved to BUY (score 88). Independent web coverage still shows the memory-driven handset downcycle grinding on into Q4 2026 before an expected 2027 recovery, so this isn't fully resolved, just re-characterized. Downgrading from persisting-RED to AMBER pending Q2 print.
flags.thesis_link: Weak/indirect match to current key_risks (handset concentration, China QCT weakness). The specific 06-30 thesis_link (memory-shortage guidance suspension) is no longer the report's stated risk profile.

evidence.source: CNBC — Qualcomm stock sinks as memory shortage drags on forecast

flags.headline: SUPV -5.85%: no identified catalyst — flagging the move itself, not a confirmed development
flags.detail: Grupo Supervielle fell -5.85% ($10.25→$9.65). Web search found no SUPV-specific negative news for this date — most recent coverage (July 10) showed the stock +7.6% and JPMorgan raising its target to $13 (Neutral) on improving Q1 profitability. This could be ADR/local-market divergence, EM/Argentina-wide flow, or a data point our sweep missed. Per guardrail #2 (never fabricate), reporting the move as unexplained rather than inventing a cause. Worth a second look if it persists.
flags.thesis_link: If it persists, would relate to SUPV key_risk #1: 'Argentine macroeconomic instability — inflation volatility, peso devaluation risk, and potential policy reversals around midterm elections.' Not confirmed this run.

flags.headline: Hyperscaler Q2 earnings window opens in 5 days (GOOG July 22) — capex commentary is the highest-priority macro signal on the book
flags.detail: Correcting the 06-30 read, which had MSFT (July 29) as the first hyperscaler print: Alphabet actually reports first, July 22, 2026 — 5 days out. Meta and Microsoft both report July 29; Amazon reports July 30. Combined 2026 hyperscaler capex guidance is now ~$725B (Alphabet $180-190B, Amazon ~$200B, Meta up to $145B, Microsoft tracking >$120B for its fiscal year) — already the subject of this week's TSMC-driven selloff. Any capex guidance revision from GOOG on the 22nd will be the first real read and will directly move CRDO, MRVL, AMD, LRCX, NVDA, KEYS, TSM, NXPI, ADI (9 of 52 holdings).

evidence.source: MarketBeat — Alphabet Q2 2026 earnings report, July 22
StockTitan — Meta to announce Q2 2026 results, July 29
MarketScreener — Amazon Q2 2026 earnings, July 30

evidence.source: Yahoo Finance — Abbott shares jump as earnings beat estimates and company raises 2026 outlook

evidence.source: StockTitan — Stryker to announce Q2 2026 results, July 30

flags.headline: STLD: the 06-30 'margin compression' AMBER appears to have been wrong — new guidance shows margin expansion; resolving
flags.detail: Steel Dynamics issued Q2 2026 EPS guidance of $3.51-$3.55/share — up sharply from Q1's $2.78 and well above prior-year Q2's $2.01. Management explicitly cites 'meaningfully higher' steel-segment profitability on strong demand and metal-margin expansion (realized prices rising faster than scrap costs), the opposite of the margin-compression narrative flagged on 06-30. A one-time $16M write-down (Arizona→Mississippi aluminum plant relocation) trims the print but is unrelated to the thesis risk. STLD's own Q2 call is July 21. Resolving the prior AMBER to green; the 06-30 flag looks to have been based on a stale or mistaken read.

evidence.source: PR Newswire — Steel Dynamics Provides Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Guidance
StockTitan — Steel Dynamics Q2 2026 call set for July 21
